items.stem: The actuarial present value of a whole life insurance of 1 payable at the end of the year of death is denoted:

options.rationale: Correct: A_x is the standard symbol for the APV of a whole life insurance.
Lowercase a with a double-dot denotes an annuity, not an insurance.
l_x is the number of lives surviving to age x in a life table.
q_x is the one-year probability of death, not an APV.

items.explanation: Correct: A_x is the standard symbol for the APV of a whole life insurance.

items.stem: Under the equivalence principle, the benefit premium is set so that:

options.text: The APV of premiums equals the APV of benefits at issue
options.rationale: Correct: the equivalence principle equates the APV of premiums and benefits.

options.text: Premiums always exceed benefits by a 20% margin
options.rationale: That describes a loading, not the pure equivalence principle.

options.text: The reserve is zero at every duration
options.rationale: Reserves are generally positive after issue.
Premiums are far smaller than the sum insured in general.

items.explanation: Correct: the equivalence principle equates the APV of premiums and benefits.

items.stem: Select TWO statements that are true about a net premium policy reserve.

options.text: It is prospectively the APV of future benefits minus the APV of future premiums
options.rationale: Correct: this is the prospective reserve definition.

options.text: It is generally zero at issue under the equivalence principle
options.rationale: Correct: at issue the APVs are equal, so the reserve is zero.
Reserves are typically non-negative after issue.

options.text: It equals the sum insured at every duration
options.rationale: The reserve builds gradually and does not equal the sum insured until maturity/death.

items.explanation: Correct: this is the prospective reserve definition.
